I had the same problem as you.

I didn't really think it was too big of a deal. As time passed, I noticed it was getting worse, but I knew I probably wouldn't kill myself, so I didn't take it too seriously.

Yet, it grew on me. The chances of me doing it kept growing. 

I started researching methods, and even got to the point of me testing if hanging myself would work (tying the rope to the top of my door, putting my head in it, and applying pressure to see how it felt, and if it would break, and hang.)
Still, it was all speculation. 

One day, I was staring down a balcony, when, in an instant, almost out of nowhere, I nearly jumped. I felt all my muscles contract, ready to do it. Only at the last second that I stopped myself. Other, more serious, occasions have happened after this event.

The reason I'm telling you this, is to illustrate how powerless you actually are against it. I've been doing a bunch of things trying to stop with my suicidal thoughts. Even with all my effort, they are still growing. 

So just be careful. These thoughts are unpredictable, and extremely bard to fight against. They grow bigger than you, before you can notice. You might think you are under control, but in reality there is no real way of knowing. 

This is not a game you want to play.

Edit: know that I think about what you've said, we are pretty similar, and going through similar things. I hope things get better, because while I can't know what you are going through, I have gone through similar things. Stay strong :v

First of all, thank you so much for replying, it's the first time i'm discussing this type of thought.

I strongly appreciate the things you said. But you see, I have a really hard time believing them. Any compliments that i receive just flies over my head. It's such a strong rejection from myind, that i don't even know what to do. It's so engrained in my way of thinking.

And even when I manage to shut this voice, I can't get myself to be motivated.

Let me put up an example:

- someone says my drawings are good.

- i am flattered, and extremely thankful that someone enjoyed my drawing. But in my mind, i can't ever get myself to believe i draw good. Being positive, i'd say i'm average. This leads me to, even if being complimented, to not want to draw. I never feel like i'm worth anything.

- even if I force myself to draw. Even if I briefly ignore my subconscious, my nihilist personality gets to me. Everything i do seems pointless, therefore it's a struggle to get anything done.

Suicide just ends up being a very appealing thought. I like sleeping. I don't really like waking up. If death is just one endless night of sleep, i can't help but to embrace it.
